title: Build CI result reuse and routing; record after-walltime vs baseline
summary: Implement build-plan items 4–7 of docs/design/ci-routing.md: a SHA-keyed CI result record with local fallback (item 4), per-job-kind routing from section 3.2 (item 5), the after-measurement using `xtask walltime` compared with the #117 baseline (item 6), and the final docs/CHANGELOG entry (item 7). Audience is the owner, who will judge by tests that fail without the behavior and a measured, honestly labeled comparison.

defaults_applied.how: All new code and tests are Rust.
New modules get tests; cargo test and clippy must pass.
Criteria check SHA mismatch, fallback, red-result behavior rather than file existence.
Judged by measured wall time per verified result with equal checks.
Docs cite sources and label unmeasured numbers as estimates.
Missing or stale CI results never count as verified.
Behavior criteria name cargo test/clippy/fmt for the verifier.
Routing and SHA rule enforced by code and tests, not prose.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The #117 baseline is the output of `xtask walltime` documented in docs/design/ci-routing-baseline.md; its real numbers may not be in the repository, so the producer must find them or recompute from available records and say which.
The after measurement needs real post-build jobs; it cannot be fully produced inside one job. I assume the deliverable is the comparison tooling plus a report stating honestly what sample exists now.
The design review is still open (the doc says so); the owner has explicitly asked to build anyway, as for items 2 and 3.
Item 7 (docs) is done last within the same job, though the design says it should be a separate job; this follows the request to finish items 4–7.
Exact Rust files are guesses from the crate layout; the producer will place the record and routing code where checks and verify logic live.
question: Where are the #117 baseline numbers recorded (file or PR)? I assumed docs/design/ci-routing-baseline.md plus job records.

acceptance_criteria.text: Tests for the CI result record pass under `cargo test --locked`: a result whose SHA differs from the candidate's is ignored; a missing/cancelled/unfinished result triggers the local fallback; a red result fails the check without the fallback masking it; a stale record never yields a verified outcome. Each test fails if the SHA comparison or fallback is removed.

Tests for routing pass: given each job kind (code, tests, docs, design, config, build, study), the routing function returns the row of section 3.2 (docs/design skip fmt/clippy but still run test; config/build never skip; unknown kind takes the config all-checks path).
`cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` are clean.
The verifier's command set in athena.toml is unchanged; Athena, not the verifier, fetches the CI record and places it in the verifier's input.

A new after-measurement doc reports median and p90 per job kind from `cargo run --locked -p xtask -- walltime`, next to the baseline from #117, with N and caveats stated. If fewer than 20 post-build jobs exist or records are unavailable, it says so rather than claiming improvement, and numbers not measured are labeled estimates.
Section 10 of docs/design/ci-routing.md marks items 4–7 with what was built and what remains; CHANGELOG.md has an entry; docs make no claim of speedup that the measurement doesn't show.
The strength guard of section 9.4 is implemented or explicitly reported: checks run per job do not fall, and reuse without SHA match counts as no improvement.

out_of_scope: Changing the cache layers or timeout-minutes beyond what measurement requires
Parallel-jobs driver and native PR landing changes
departures: Request bundles four build-plan items including real code, routing config, and a measurement that depends on post-build job data; far larger than the typical job, so cost, time and pass probability are worse than the reference.
